acceptance: The boundary step list holds no step for `evolve ci latency check`
A test fails when any boundary step names a verb or sub-verb that the binary does not register; the test is red before the fix
`evolve boundary run --dry-run` prints no step that exits with a usage error
fix: Remove the `ci latency check` step from the boundary step list in go/cmd/evolve/cmd_boundary.go. Keep the `wave latency --check` step. Add one test that resolves the verb and the first argument of every boundary step against the registered verbs of the binary, so a step that names a missing verb fails the build.
summary: go/cmd/evolve/cmd_boundary.go:237 runs the advisory step `evolve ci latency check` at each boundary. The verb does not exist: `evolve ci` has classify, watch, darwin-set and telemetry only. The T5 item that would build it (latency-gates-t5-ci-trend-gate) was withdrawn by the operator. So the step fails at each boundary and the failure is hidden because the step is advisory. A boundary step that always fails hides a real fault when one occurs. Source: docs/plans/latency-gates-2026-10.md, row T7 (partial).
title: The boundary run no longer calls the verb `evolve ci latency check`, which does not exist
